lawyer:
Md. Hannan with AKM Ali and M Khaled Ahmed, Advocates ------ For the Petitioner.  
Akhtar Imam, Advocate ------ For the Respondent Nos. 1-2
parties:
Shamsuddin Ahmed alias Md. Shamsuddin  ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Managing Director, Bangladesh Mukti Juddha Kallyan Trust and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Jalil, J. : This Rule was issued against an order dated 26.9.91 passed by the Secretary, Bangladesh Mukti Juddha Kallyan Trust terminating the service of the petitioner as Deputy Chief Accountant of the Trust. 

 2. The case of the petitioner is that he was appointed as Deputy Manager (Computer) in the Mukti Juddha Kallayan Trust on 5.12.1987 and was confirmed in that post after satisfactory completion of probationary period with effect from 5.12.87. Thereafter he was promoted to the post of Manager (Computer) of the said Trust at its Head Office in the pay scale of Tk. 3700.00-4825.00 per month with other benefits, a copy which has been filed by the petitioner as Annexure 'C' to the petition. Thereafter he was transferred to the Finance Division as Deputy Chief Accountant on 11.2.90. While he was serving as such his service was terminated by the impugned order. It is the further case of the petitioner that the petitioner's service having been terminated on the ground of being surplus the service of the person holding the same rank and junior to him should have been terminated but the petitioner has been selected with malafide motive and that the petitioner is not the junior most in the same rank but there are some other officers working in the same rank who are junior to him and as such the order was passed arbitrarily and without lawful authority. 

 3. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2, namely, Managing Director and the Secretary, Bangladesh Mukti Juddha Kallyan Trust filed an affidavit-in-opposition controverting the material allegation and contending that the petitioner was the junior most of the three Deputy Chief Accountants in the Head Office, Finance Division against two such posts as per Organigram of the Trust Head Office and as such his service was properly terminated as a surplus personnel and that there is no uniform practice or statutory rules that the junior most officer should be terminated in such cases and so the order was not malafide. 

 4. The petitioner filed an affidavit-in-reply to the said affidavit-in-opposition denying the material allegation and maintaining his stand taken in the writ petition. It has further been stated in the affidavit-in-reply that the petitioner was promoted to the substantive grade on 1.4.89 with designation of Manager (Computer) and two other persons and one Sanaullah Chowdhury were promoted in the said substantive grade on 1.5.89 who was junior to the petitioner and that one Mr. Yusuf Ali Miah is a direct appointee in the same grade and scale having been appointed on 4.4.90 is also junior to the petitioner by 9 months. Under the Service Rules of the Trust an employee may be transferred to any post provided that his basic pay is not thereby actually reduced. The post of Deputy Chief Accountant and of Manager (Computer) being in the same grade and scale are always inter-transferable and that there are several vacant posts in the Trust of the grade and scale of the petitioner. 

 6. Mr. Akhtar Imam, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 1 and 2, on the other hand, submits that out of three Deputy Chief Accountants the petitioner is the junior most and only two posts of Deputy Chief Accountants are sanctioned, so the petitioner having been surplus he was rightly terminated and that there is no malafide in it. He further submits that the impugned order was passed without any malafide motive so the writ petition does not lie. 

 So this Rule has given power to the authority to terminate the service of any person without assigning any reason. In the impugned order some reasons have been given that the petitioner's service was terminated as a surplus person. As some reason has been assigned that reason must be justified whatever may be in the Rule. The authority cannot pick and choose as it likes at any time. It is the case of the petitioner that he is not junior most as alleged. The petitioner has filed a copy of an order giving promotion to various officers in the said Trust of different grades. The authenticity of this letter has not been questioned which is marked as Annexure 'C' to the petition. It appears that the petitioner Md. Shamsuddin was promoted as Manager (Computer) from the post of Deputy Manager (Computer) in the Head Officer with effect from 1.4.89 and in the same grade there are other persons who were also promoted to the same grade and are shown below him and one Sanaullah Chowdhury who was Assistant Deputy Chief Accountant was promoted as Deputy Chief Accountant on 1.5.89 and he is still serving which has not been denied. It is to be mentioned that the petitioner was transferred from the post of Manager (Computer) to the post of Deputy Chief Accountant so the posts bearing the same scale of pay and of the same grade are inter-transferable, under the general rule the junior most person of the same grade should be retrenched or terminated first. In the affidavit-in- opposition it has been stated that there were three Deputy Chief Accountants in the Head Office against 2 sanctioned posts and one became surplus and the petitioner being the junior most in that post his service was terminated. This statement is not acceptable as he may be junior in the post of Deputy Chief Accountants having been transferred later than the two others, but in order to determine the seniority the date of appointment/promotion of all officers working in the same grade, namely, as Manager and Deputy Chief Accountants should be considered which are inter-transferable and the petitioner was transferred from the post of Manager to the post of Deputy Chief Accountant. If appears that the petitioner is now aged about 38 years and at this stage of life he is going to be thrown out and so before such a drastic action was taken it should have been considered as to whether he is actually junior most in the same grade. The petitioner has filed a copy of the resolution of the Bangladesh Freedom Fighters' Welfare Trust wherefrom it appears that 50% officers and staff of Head Office were to be terminated on the principle of last come first out except Freedom Fighters (Annexure X to the affidavit-in-reply). This resolution was passed on 30th August, 1980 and long thereafter the petitioner was promoted as Manager (Computer) in 1989. Be that as it may, the principle of last come first out rule should have been followed before terminating the service of the petitioner but it was not followed.
